nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a real $n \times n$ matrix with singular values $\sigma_0 \ge \sigma_1 \ge \dots$ on Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$, indexed from $0$ and extended by zeros, where $n - 1$ is read as $0$ when $n = 0$. If $\sigma_{n-1} \ne 0$, then the condition number of $A$ equals $\sigma_0 / \sigma_{n-1}$.
nodes.title: Condition number as a singular-value ratio

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a real $n \times n$ matrix with singular values $\sigma_0 \ge \sigma_1 \ge \dots$ on Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$, indexed from $0$ and extended by zeros, where $n - 1$ is read as $0$ when $n = 0$. If $\sigma_{n-1} = 0$, then the condition number of $A$ is $\infty$.
nodes.title: Infinite condition number from a vanishing singular value

nodes.summary: The condition number of the $1 \times 1$ real identity matrix is $1$.
nodes.title: Condition number of the order-one identity

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the condition number of the real $n \times n$ zero matrix is $\infty$; this includes the $0 \times 0$ matrix.
nodes.title: The zero matrix has infinite condition number

nodes.summary: For a real $n \times n$ matrix $A$, let $\sigma_0 \ge \sigma_1 \ge \dots$ be the singular values of $A$ acting on Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$, indexed from $0$ and extended by $\sigma_i = 0$ for $i \ge n$. The condition number of $A$, an element of $[0, \infty]$, is $\infty$ if $\sigma_{n-1} = 0$ and $\sigma_0 / \sigma_{n-1}$ otherwise, where $n - 1$ is read as $0$ when $n = 0$.
nodes.title: Condition number of a square real matrix

nodes.summary: The decay exponent is the supremum, taken in the extended reals $[-\infty, \infty]$, of the set of admissible exponents $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Decay exponent of minimum sign-matrix condition numbers

nodes.summary: If $C$ is a real $n \times n$ symmetric conference matrix and $I$ is the $n \times n$ identity matrix, then there is a Boolean $n \times n$ matrix whose realization as a real sign matrix equals $C + I$.
nodes.title: Adding the identity to a symmetric conference matrix gives a sign matrix

nodes.summary: Send each $n \times n$ Boolean matrix to the real matrix whose entry is $-1$ where the Boolean entry is true and $1$ where it is false. A real $n \times n$ matrix $M$ arises in this way if and only if every entry of $M$ is $1$ or $-1$.
nodes.title: Boolean matrices realize exactly the sign matrices

nodes.summary: The Hadamard hypothesis is the proposition that for every natural number $n$ divisible by $4$ there is an $n \times n$ Hadamard matrix with integer entries, that is, an integer matrix $H$ with all entries $\pm 1$ such that $H H^{\mathsf{T}} = H^{\mathsf{T}} H = n I$.
nodes.title: Hadamard hypothesis

nodes.summary: A real number $\alpha$ is an admissible exponent when there is a subpolynomial sequence $f \colon \mathbb{N} \to [0, \infty)$ such that for every positive integer $n$ the minimum condition number $\kappa_n$ of the real $n \times n$ sign matrices satisfies $\kappa_n = 1 + f(n) / n^{\alpha}$, as an equality in $[0, \infty]$.
nodes.title: Admissible decay exponents

nodes.summary: A sequence $f \colon \mathbb{N} \to [0, \infty)$ is subpolynomial when for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ we have $f(n) = o(n^{\varepsilon})$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Subpolynomial sequences

nodes.summary: A real $n \times n$ matrix $C$ is a symmetric conference matrix when $n \ge 2$, $C^{\mathsf{T}} = C$, every diagonal entry of $C$ is $0$, every off-diagonal entry of $C$ is $1$ or $-1$, and $C C^{\mathsf{T}} = (n - 1) I$, where $I$ is the identity matrix.
nodes.title: Symmetric conference matrices

nodes.summary: For every positive integer $n$, there is an $n \times n$ Boolean matrix whose realization as a real sign matrix ($-1$ for true, $1$ for false) has condition number equal to the minimum condition number of order $n$.
nodes.title: The minimum condition number is attained

nodes.summary: The minimum condition number of order $1$ is $1$: the least condition number of a $1 \times 1$ real sign matrix is $1$.
nodes.title: Minimum condition number of order one

nodes.summary: For a positive integer $n$, the minimum condition number of order $n$ is the least condition number of a real $n \times n$ sign matrix, that is, a matrix all of whose entries are $1$ or $-1$; the minimum is taken over the finitely many such matrices.
nodes.title: Minimum condition number of sign matrices

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every real $n \times n$ matrix $A$, the condition number of $A$ is at least $1$.
nodes.title: Condition numbers are at least one

nodes.summary: For every positive integer $n$, the minimum condition number of the real $n \times n$ sign matrices is at least $1$.
nodes.title: The minimum condition number is at least one

nodes.summary: For every Boolean $n \times n$ matrix $A$ and all indices $i, j$, the $(i, j)$ entry of the real realization of $A$ is $1$ or $-1$.
nodes.title: Realized sign matrices have entries $\pm 1$

nodes.summary: The realization of a Boolean $n \times n$ matrix $A$ is the real $n \times n$ matrix whose $(i, j)$ entry is $-1$ if $A_{ij}$ is true and $1$ if $A_{ij}$ is false.
nodes.title: Real sign matrix of a Boolean matrix

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, a sign matrix of order $n$ is encoded as an $n \times n$ matrix with entries in the Booleans $\{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$, whose rows and columns are indexed by $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$.
nodes.title: Boolean encoding of sign matrices

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
